newsitem.title: USA: Ecuador sugar output set to rise - U.S. attache.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador sugar output set to rise - U.S. attache.

text.p: Ecuador's sugar production for 1997-98 is forecast to rise to 466,000 tonnes, the highest level in twenty years, according to a U.S. attache report made public on Wednesday by the U.S. Agriculture Department.
Ecuador will produce an estimated 451,000 tonnes in the 1996-97 marketing year, the report said.

"New investments in the sugar industry, coupled with favorable weather conditions, have combined to boost the production levels," the report said. The country has become a net sugar exporter as a result of recent production increases.
During the next three to five years, "exports could reach 60,000 tonnes or more with the addition of modern refining capacity," the attache report said.
Attache reports released by the Agriculture Department are not official USDA projections.
